fatal_errors: The proposed material is an additively manufactured, coarse-grained single-phase HEA rather than the as-cast lamellar L12/B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy.
The comparison substitutes inert-versus-chloride exposure for the target comparison with identically conditioned duplex stainless steel 2205 in deionized water.
It omits the rapid 1100 °C thermal-shock treatment and the governing temperature dependence, including the minimum degradation near 50 °C.

The proposed nanocrystalline/amorphous-layer and inverse Hall–Petch mechanism is not the target competition among depassivation, repassivation, tribolayer stability, abrasion, and oxide-layer disruption.
The chloride-rich environment and localized-corrosion prediction are unsupported by the cited evidence and lie outside the target test environment.
explanation: The response addresses coupled mechanical and electrochemical degradation and offers a testable surface-transformation hypothesis, so it is a scientifically plausible alternative rather than an exact reconstruction. Its paired experiment includes useful structural, chemical, electrochemical, friction, and wear measurements. However, the inert and aqueous tests also change lubrication and contact mechanics, so they do not isolate chemical reactivity alone; an aqueous chloride-free control would be needed. The hypothesis fails to recover nearly every target-specific element: the eutectic L12/B2 alloy, DS2205 comparator, thermal-shock conditioning, deionized-water tests over 25–100 °C, and the nonmonotonic wear minimum at 50 °C. E2 gives limited support for tribologically induced refinement and oxidation effects in a different additively manufactured HEA, while E1 is only generic background. Neither citation establishes chloride-induced localized corrosion of the proposed tribolayer. The falsification rule is directionally useful but overly conjunctive, because failure of any one predicted signature should be interpreted separately rather than requiring all signatures to be absent.
